build.title: Builds share one Claude login and write refreshed tokens back

said.text: Brett: 'they're supposed to, it's supposed to write the new refresh token to the same place in whatever account, whatever build uses the next updates the refresh token.' Right now each build gets its own saved copy of the account login (log shows 'own copy (saved)'), so when one copy refreshes, the rotated refresh token kills every other copy. demo-video-series-three-minute-browser died with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' on mossesx-max. Fix: every build uses the account's one shared credentials file, and any refreshed token is written back there under a lock. Phone alert on any auth failure; re-queue the failed build once login works.

# Build: builds-share-one-claude-login-write

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Builds share one Claude login and write refreshed tokens back" (builds-share-one-claude-login-write) [orchestrator] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (6 left, ~1.8 h):
[ ] s1 (~20 min) Find where build sessions copy the account login; switch them to the one shared credentials file per account
[ ] s2 (~20 min) Write refreshed tokens back to the shared file under a lock so parallel builds don't clobber each other
[ ] s3 (~15 min) Test two builds on one account: force a refresh in one, confirm the other keeps working
[ ] s4 (~15 min) Phone alert on any OAuth failure and auto re-queue the failed build once the login works
[ ] s5 (~20 min) Phone notifications through AmberX for every login event: one each time a build signs in / uses the account token (which account, which build, verified OK or failed), and one each time the token is refreshed confirming the new token was saved to the shared file successfully (or that it failed). Brett: 'I want a verification every time it uses the token... and then a notification to tell me that it was successfully refreshed and changed.'
[ ] s6 (~20 min) Any queued build that tries to launch and fails (any reason: auth, slot, crash, launcher error) sends an AmberX phone alert right away with the build name and the exact reason it failed. Brett: 'anytime something gets in the queue and it attempts to run and it fails, I want an alert and I want to know why.'
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step builds-share-one-claude-login-write <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link builds-share-one-claude-login-write --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step builds-share-one-claude-login-write <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note builds-share-one-claude-login-write "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.
